Ana (Product): quick post-all-hands note — two recurring customer asks that came up in Q&A re: rate limits/credits/packaging. jotting them here for the docs/FAQ: (A) what's the difference between request throttling vs credit exhaustion? (B) how do retries/backoff affect billing?

Leo (CEO): short framing: throttling (429s) is an enforcement decision; credits are a billing meter. They interact but are separate: you can be throttled without billing impact, and you can burn credits without being throttled if capacity allows.

Ravi (SRE): more detail from runtime: we have three levers — ingress throttle (per-org rps/concurrency), burst reservoir (hosted prepay credits or reserved headroom), and emission accounting (tokens billed at "emit"). In practice: ingress checks reject early; only requests that reach the model and cause token emission incur charges.

Marta (Finance): can someone confirm whether streamed partial responses consume credits as they arrive or only when the stream completes? customers ask this a lot.

Ravi (SRE): streamed responses are billed incrementally as tokens are emitted. if a client closes mid-stream those already-emitted tokens are billed; future tokens are not.

Tori (Support): customers also confused about retries — they see duplicate charges after a retry, what should we tell them?

Ravi (SRE): retries risk double-emission if the original request was delivered but the client timed out before receiving the response. recommend clients use idempotency-key header for non-streaming requests and prefer client-side cancellation when possible.

Ana (Product): proposed customer FAQ snippet: "If you receive a 429 that's a rate enforcement signal; no tokens are billed unless the model emitted output. For hosted plans we provide a short burst buffer which can temporarily serve extra RPS and consume prepay credits; for Dedicated plans small bursts may be absorbed by reserved capacity per your contract. Retries can increase token use if duplicate requests reach the model — use idempotency keys and client cancelation to avoid this."

Marta (Finance): also note: billing cadence differs: hosted prepay credits are deducted in near-real time; invoiced accounts get a monthly invoice. Dedicated contracts usually have committed spend + negotiated overage terms; we surface alerts for overages before invoicing.

Tori (Support): can we get a one-liner we can paste into Zendesk? short pls.

Ana (Product): paste-ready one-liner: "429 = throttled; tokens only billed when the model emits. Hosted bursts may consume credits; Dedicated bursts usually use reserved capacity. Send your org id if you'd like us to check."

Ravi (SRE): internal note for engs: add a runtime metric 'billing_point' with values 'on_emit' or 'on_complete' depending on model path. default is 'on_emit'. we should also emit 'retry_duplicate_emissions' counter to monitor customer impact.

Ana (Product): action list: 1) @Ravi add metrics + open PR to docs with exact defaults (burst window, default rps), 2) @Marta confirm overage alert thresholds + messaging, 3) @Tori add one-liner to Zendesk, 4) @DocsBot link the PR once ready.

DocsBot: created docs PR -> https://git.redwood.internal/docs/pull/4207 (faq + metrics proposal).

Ana (Product): thanks — leaving this thread open for any nuance or phrasing suggestions before we publish.
